arxiv-1410-0837.title: Asymptotic Representations of Quantum Affine Superalgebras
arxiv-1410-0837.creator: Huafeng ZHANG
arxiv-1410-0837.description: Abstract We study representations of the quantum affine superalgebra associated with a general linear Lie superalgebra. In the spirit of Hernandez–Jimbo, we construct inductive systems of Kirillov–Reshetikhin modules based on a cyclicity result that we established previously on tensor products of these modules, and realize their inductive limits as modules over its Borel subalgebra, the so-called q q -Yangian.

arxiv-2009-06337.title: Towards an RDF Knowledge Graph of Scholars from Early Modern History
arxiv-2009-06337.creator: Jennifer Blanke, Thomas Riechert
arxiv-2009-06337.description: Abstract The use of Semantic Web Technologies supports research in the field of digital humanities. In this paper we focus on the creation of semantic independent online databases such as those of historical prosopography. These databases contain biographical information of historical persons.

arxiv-2104-13032.title: High contrast imaging at 10 microns, a search for exoplanets around: Eps Indi A, Eps Eri, Tau Ceti, Sirius A and Sirius B
arxiv-2104-13032.creator: P. Pathak, D. J. M. Petit dit de la Roche, M. Kasper, M. Sterzik, O. Absil ,, A. Boehle, F. Feng, V. D. Ivanov, M. Janson, H.R.A. Jones, A. Kaufer, H.-U. Käufl, A.-L. Maire, M. Meyer, E. Pantin, R. Siebenmorgen, M. E. van den Ancker, G. Viswanath
arxiv-2104-13032.description: Abstract Context. The direct imaging of rocky exoplanets is one of the major science goals for upcoming large telescopes. The contrast requirement for imaging such planets is challenging. However, the mid-IR (InfraRed) regime provides the optimum contrast to directly detect the thermal signatures of exoplanets in our solar neighbourhood. Aims.

arxiv-2201-02681.title: Existence of solutions for a bi-species kinetic model of a cylindrical Langmuir probe
arxiv-2201-02681.creator: M. Badsi, L. Godard-Cadillac
arxiv-2201-02681.description: Abstract In this article, we study a collisionless kinetic model for plasmas in the neighborhood of a cylindrical metallic Langmuir probe. This model consists in a bi-species Vlasov-Poisson equation in a domain contained between two cylinders with prescribed boundary conditions. The interior cylinder models the probe while the exterior cylinder models the interaction with the plasma core.

arxiv-2205-02450.title: Pessimism meets VCG: Learning Dynamic Mechanism Design via Offline Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2205-02450.creator: Boxiang Lyu, Zhaoran Wang, Mladen Kolar, Zhuoran Yang
arxiv-2205-02450.description: Abstract Dynamic mechanism design has garnered significant attention from both computer scientists and economists in recent years. By allowing agents to interact with the seller over multiple rounds, where agents’ reward functions may change with time and are state-dependent, the framework is able to model a rich class of real-world problems.

arxiv-2212-01341.title: SO(1,3) Yang–Mills solutions on Minkowski space via cosets kaushal.kumar224@gmail.com
arxiv-2212-01341.description: Abstract We present a novel family of Yang–Mills solutions, with gauge group SO(1,3), on Minkowski space that are geometrically distinguished into two classes, viz. interior and exterior of the lightcone. We achieve this by foliating the former with SO(1,3)/SO(3) cosets and the latter with SO(1,3)/SO(1,2) cosets and analytically solving the Yang–Mills equation of an SO(1,3)-invariant gauge field.

arxiv-2301-10580.title: A Mathematical Programming approach to Overlapping community detection by cluster’s Shapley value
arxiv-2301-10580.creator: Stefano Benati, Justo Puerto, Antonio M. Rodríguez-Chía, Francisco Temprano
arxiv-2301-10580.description: Abstract We propose a new model to detect the overlapping communities of a network that is based on cooperative games and mathematical programming. More specifically, communities are defined as stable coalitions of a weighted graph community game and they are revealed as the optimal solution of a mixed-integer linear programming problem.

arxiv-2312-08655.title: The small 𝒌 𝐓 k_{\rm T} region in Drell-Yan production at next-to-leading order with the Parton Branching Method
arxiv-2312-08655.creator: I. Bubanja, A. Bermudez Martinez, L. Favart, F. Guzman, F. Hautmann, H. Jung, A. Lelek, M. Mendizabal, K. Moral Figueroa, L. Moureaux, N. Raicevic, M. Seidel, S. Taheri Monfared

Raicevic, M. Seidel, S. Taheri Monfared. The Parton Branching (PB) method describes the evolution of transverse momentum dependent (TMD) parton distributions, covering all kinematic regions from small to large transverse momenta k T k_{\rm T} .

arxiv-2401-05206.title: Tailoring Frictional Properties of Surfaces Using Diffusion Models
arxiv-2401-05206.creator: Even Marius Nordhagen, Henrik Andersen Sveinsson, Anders Malthe-Sørenssen
arxiv-2401-05206.description: Abstract This Letter introduces an approach for precisely designing surface friction properties using a conditional generative machine learning model, specifically a diffusion denoising probabilistic model (DDPM). We created a dataset of synthetic surfaces with frictional properties determined by molecular dynamics simulations, which trained the DDPM to predict surface structures from desired frictional outcomes.

arxiv-2406-02547.title: Leveraging Visual Tokens for Extended Text Contexts in Multi-Modal Learning
arxiv-2406-02547.creator: Alex Jinpeng Wang, Linjie Li, Yiqi Lin, Min Li, Lijuan Wang, Mike Zheng Shou, [3pt] Show Lab, National University of Singapore
arxiv-2406-02547.description: Abstract Training models with longer in-context lengths is a significant challenge for multimodal model due to substantial GPU memory and computational costs. This exploratory study does not present state-of-the-art models; rather, it introduces an innovative method designed to increase in-context text length in multi-modality large language models (MLLMs) efficiently.

arxiv-2407-19393.title: Integrating Cognitive AI with Generative Models for Enhanced Question Answering in Skill-based Learning
arxiv-2407-19393.creator: Rochan H. Madhusudhana, Rahul K. Dass, Jeanette Luu, Ashok K. Goel
arxiv-2407-19393.description: Abstract In online learning, the ability to provide quick and accurate feedback to learners is crucial. In skill-based learning, learners need to understand the underlying concepts and mechanisms of a skill to be able to apply it effectively. While videos are a common tool in online learning, they cannot comprehend or assess the skills being taught.

arxiv-2502-14163.title: "It Brought the Model to Life": Exploring the Embodiment of Multimodal I3Ms for People who are Blind or have Low Vision Conference: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; April 26-May 1, 2025; Yokohama, Japan CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI ’25), April 26-May
arxiv-2502-14163.creator: Samuel Reinders, Matthew Butler, Kim Marriott
arxiv-2502-14163.description: Abstract . 3D-printed models are increasingly used to provide people who are blind or have low vision (BLV) with access to maps, educational materials, and museum exhibits. Recent research has explored interactive 3D-printed models (I3Ms) that integrate touch gestures, conversational dialogue, and haptic vibratory feedback to create more engaging interfaces.

arxiv-2505-18898.title: Absence of Long - Range Order and Magnetic Anisotropy in the Triangular Magnet NdMgAl 11 O 19
arxiv-2505-18898.creator: Sonu Kumar, Gaël Bastien, Jan Prokleška, Mateusz Kempiński, Wojciech Kempiński, Karol Załęski, Andrej Kancko, Cinthia Antunes Corrêa, T. Treu, P. Gegenwart, Małgorzata Śliwińska-Bartkowiak, Ross H. Colman
arxiv-2505-18898.description: Abstract We investigated the rare-earth triangular-lattice antiferromagnet NdMgAl 11 O 19 using single-crystal magnetization (1.8 K ≤ T ≤ \leq~T~\leq 300 K, μ 0 ​ H ≤ 7 \mu_{0}H\leq 7 T) and specific-heat measurements down to 45 mK. The dc susceptibility confirms a well-isolated Kramers doublet ground state with pronounced Ising-type anisotropy, with g c ≈ 3.7 g_{c}\approx 3.

pmc-10484994.title: Coordination of alternative splicing and alternative polyadenylation revealed by targeted long read sequencing
pmc-10484994.creator: Zhiping Zhang, Bongmin Bae, Winston H. Dredge, Pedro Miura
pmc-10484994.description: Nervous system development is associated with extensive regulation of alternative splicing (AS) and alternative polyadenylation (APA). AS and APA have been extensively studied in isolation, but little is known about how these processes are coordinated. Here, the coordination of cassette exon (CE) splicing and APA in Drosophila was investigated using a targeted long-read sequencing approach we call Pull-a-Long-Seq (PL-Seq).

pmc-10661870.title: The Effects of Antioxidants and Pulsed Magnetic Fields on Slow and Fast Skeletal Muscle Atrophy Induced by Streptozotocin: A Preclinical Study
pmc-10661870.creator: Bora Tastekin, Aykut Pelit, Tugce Sapmaz, Alper Celenk, Muhammed Majeed, Lakshmi Mundkur, Kalyanam Nagabhushanam
pmc-10661870.description: Results Our findings suggest that antioxidants and PMF may alleviate impaired protein synthesis and degradation pathways in skeletal muscle atrophy. PTS showed a positive effect on the anabolic pathway, while RSV and PMF demonstrated potential for ameliorating the catabolic pathway.

pmc-11663961.title: Achieving desired characteristic impedances in customized coplanar waveguide transmission line design
pmc-11663961.creator: Mohd H. S Alrashdan
pmc-11663961.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Coplanar waveguide (CPW) transmission lines are valued for their planar design, low radiation, and minimized signal loss, but controlling their characteristic impedance remains a challenge. This study employs the Taguchi method, a statistical approach, to optimize the characteristic impedance by adjusting eight control factors: track width, track thickness, gap width, dielectric height, backplane thickness, conductor material conductivity, dielectric conductivity, and operational frequency.

pmc-12935487.title: Experimental Designs for Preclinical Neuroscience Experiments: Part 2—Blocking and Blocked Designs
pmc-12935487.creator: P. S. Reynolds
pmc-12935487.description: Blocking is a key statistical method introduced almost a century ago by Ronald Fisher. Blocking controls the effect of “nuisance” variables that are not of direct interest but introduce unwanted variation into the experimental response. Block factors, such as cage, litter, or time, are used to group experimental units into homogeneous subsets.

pmc-13232910.title: Dexmedetomidine versus usual care in adult patients with septic shock receiving vasopressors
pmc-13232910.creator: Isaac B Wolfkind, Luke T Geftos, William K Mitchell, Ronan J McOsker, Jose L Puglisi, Baljit S Gill
pmc-13232910.description: BACKGROUNDSeptic shock is characterised by sepsis-induced hypotension refractory to fluid resuscitation efforts. Further treatment often requires mechanical ventilation, typically requiring the use of sedatives to provide analgesia, sedation and anxiolysis. One sedative, dexmedetomidine, is an α2 agonist that has demonstrated potential in improving haemodynamic and clinical outcomes in recent randomised controlled trials.
